bmt-2018-spring-power-02.prompt:
A *graph* has a set of vertices and a set of edges, each edge joining two distinct vertices (at most one edge between two vertices). Two vertices are *neighbors* if an edge joins them. A *path* is a sequence of distinct vertices $v_0,v_1,\dots,v_k$ in which consecutive vertices are neighbors. A *cycle* is a path $v_1,\dots,v_k$ with $k\ge3$ in which $v_1$ and $v_k$ are also neighbors. A graph is *connected* if there is a path between any two of its vertices. A *tree* is a graph on $n\ge2$ vertices in which for any two vertices $u,v$ there is exactly one path from $u$ to $v$. The *degree* of a vertex is its number of neighbors, and a *leaf* is a vertex of degree $1$.

Find the longest path in the following graph.
bmt-2018-spring-power-02.answer: The path $7,6,2,3,5$ (or its reverse $5,3,2,6,7$), with $5$ vertices.
